questions.def: "Several" means more than two, but not a large number.
questions.question: ___ students passed the exam, but not all.

questions.def: "Further" means additional information; "farther" is distance.
questions.question: I need ___ information before I decide.

questions.def: "Fewer" is used for countable nouns, like "people".
questions.question: There were ___ people at the meeting than expected.

questions.def: "Neither" means not one nor the other (two options).
questions.question: ___ of the applicants had the required experience.

questions.def: "Some" indicates a portion of a group.
questions.question: ___ of us is going to the party tonight.

questions.def: After "every" use a singular noun: "Every student".
questions.question: Every students in the class passed the test.

questions.def: "Much" is used with uncountable nouns, like "time".
questions.question: I don't have ___ time to finish the project.

questions.def: "Most of" is used with uncountable nouns like "information."
questions.question: ___ of the information was useful for my research.

questions.def: "A great deal" is used with uncountable nouns like "money".
questions.question: He spent ___ of his money on the new car.

questions.def: "Fewer" is correct with countable nouns like "people".
questions.question: Less people attended the conference this year.

questions.def: "Other" is used for plural nouns without specifying.
questions.question: We need to consider ___ options before deciding.

questions.def: "Several" is for more than two, but not all.
questions.question: ___ of the paintings were by Van Gogh.

questions.def: "Most of" requires "the" before a specific noun.
questions.question: ___ the students passed the test.

questions.def: "Little" expresses a lack of hope (uncountable).
questions.question: There is ___ hope of finding them alive.

questions.def: "None" means not one of the books.
questions.question: ___ of the books on the shelf are mine.

questions.def: "A wealth of" means a large amount of experience.
questions.question: He has ___ experience in this field.

questions.def: "Number" is used with countable nouns like "people".
questions.question: A large ___ of people attended the concert.

questions.def: "Each" emphasizes individuality within a group.
questions.question: ___ child needs individual attention.

questions.def: "Neither" refers to two options, none suitable.
questions.question: ___ of the candidates was suitable.

questions.def: "Whole" describes the entirety of the day.
questions.question: I spent the ___ day reading.

questions.def: "All of" specifies a group after "all".
questions.question: ___ the students have finished their exams.

questions.def: "A good deal of" used with uncountable nouns.
questions.question: He has ___ knowledge of the subject.

questions.def: "Certain" means specific but not named.
questions.question: There are ___ things I need to do.

questions.def: "Few" is used with countable nouns like "applicants".
questions.question: ___ of the applicants were qualified.

questions.def: "A little" is used for uncountable nouns (sugar) meaning some.
questions.question: I need ___ sugar for the recipe.

questions.def: "Other" is used to indicate an alternative.
questions.question: I have no ___ choice but to accept.

questions.def: "Several of" needs the "of" when referring to a specific group.
questions.question: ___ the students were late to class.

questions.def: "Some" is used for uncountable nouns like advice.
questions.question: He needs ___ advice from a professional.

questions.def: "Few" implies almost none, fitting the negative implication.
questions.question: ___ of the applicants had the required experience.

questions.def: "Further" means additional in a non-physical sense.
questions.question: I need ___ information before making a decision.
